submissionRequirements.title: Title & Abstract
submissionRequirements.text: A concise title and an abstract (max 300 words).

submissionRequirements.title: Session Track
submissionRequirements.text: Clear indication of Paper with Workshop or Paper without Workshop.

submissionRequirements.title: Outline & Schedule
submissionRequirements.text: A breakdown of how the allotted time will be used.
items: Papers with workshop: detailed breakdown of the 25-minute morning session and milestone-based progression for the 90-minute workshop.
Papers without workshop: clear breakdown of the 15-minute presentation structure.

submissionRequirements.title: Prerequisites & Toolchain (Papers with Workshop)
submissionRequirements.text: List of required software, target OS compatibility, hardware dependencies, and recommended skill level.

submissionRequirements.title: Workshop Size (Papers with Workshop)
submissionRequirements.text: Choose a workshop for 25 or 50 participants. If the workshop needs equipment, prepare 10 sets for 25 participants or 20 sets for 50 participants.

submissionRequirements.title: Participant Hardware Requirements (Papers with Workshop)
submissionRequirements.text: The minimum hardware participants' laptops must meet, such as CPU, memory (RAM), GPU, free disk space and operating system. These requirements are published to attendees.

submissionRequirements.title: Teaching Assistant (Papers with Workshop)
submissionRequirements.text: At least one teaching assistant (TA) to help participants during the practical part of the workshop.

submissionRequirements.title: Interactive Demo Video (Papers with Workshop only)
submissionRequirements.text: A short demonstration video (2–5 minutes) showcasing the functioning prototype, project workflow, or target outcomes participants will build during the workshop.
items: Please provide a publicly viewable or unlisted link (e.g., YouTube, Vimeo, Loom, or Google Drive).
This video is crucial for the program committee to evaluate technical feasibility and participant engagement.

submissionRequirements.title: Speaker Bio
submissionRequirements.text: Professional background (max 150 words), previous speaking experience, and relevant project links (e.g., GitHub, Google Scholar, LinkedIn).

items.q: What can I submit to ICAS?
items.a: Two kinds of proposals: Papers with Workshop (5 speaking slots), which engage the audience interactively through a presentation and a workshop, and Papers without Workshop (8 speaking slots), which present academic work relevant to the conference theme. Calls for special sessions, tutorials, live demonstrations and the grand challenge will be announced separately.

items.q: What is the difference between the two tracks?
items.a: Speakers of papers with workshop give a 25-minute presentation in the morning and run a 90-minute workshop in the afternoon. Speakers of papers without workshop give a talk of about 15 minutes in sessions that run concurrently with the afternoon workshops.

items.q: Does my topic have to match the conference theme?
items.a: Submissions aligned with the conference theme are warmly welcomed, but topics are not strictly limited to it: any compelling, relevant research is welcome. The theme places particular emphasis on implementation, such as robotics, vehicles and embedded systems.

items.q: In which language must proposals be written?
items.a: All submissions must be in English.

items.q: What must a proposal contain?
items.a: A title and an abstract of at most 300 words, the session track, an outline and schedule, and a speaker bio of at most 150 words with previous speaking experience and relevant project links. Papers with workshop also need the prerequisites and toolchain, the workshop size, the laptop hardware requirements for participants, the teaching assistant(s) and a 2–5 minute demo video.

items.q: Which video platforms can I use for the demo video?
items.a: Any service that gives a publicly viewable or unlisted link, for example YouTube, Vimeo, Loom or Google Drive. Make sure the link works without signing in.

items.q: Is the review double-blind?
items.a: Yes. Proposals undergo double-blind peer review. Keep names and affiliations out of the title, abstract and outline; speaker details are collected in a separate part of the submission form.

items.q: How are proposals evaluated?
items.a: On technical depth and originality, clarity and feasibility (particularly for 90-minute workshops), the engagement plan, and alignment with current industry and academic trends.

items.q: Do I have to use the ICAS slide template?
items.a: Yes. All speakers of accepted papers, with or without workshop, must prepare their presentation slides with the official ICAS slide template, available on the Presentation Guidelines page.

items.q: How does the 40% speaker feedback work?
items.a: Speakers of papers with workshop receive feedback based on attendance: 40% of the registration fees of their workshop. An engaging topic that draws more participants results in more feedback.

items.q: How large is a workshop?
items.a: Speakers choose a workshop for 25 or 50 participants. If the workshop needs equipment, speakers prepare 10 sets for 25 participants or 20 sets for 50 participants.

items.q: Who provides the equipment for a workshop?
items.a: Speakers are responsible for preparing all necessary equipment and environment set-ups for the workshop. Attendees are asked to bring their own laptops.

items.q: What hardware do participants need?
items.a: Speakers provide the laptop hardware requirements of their workshop (for example CPU, memory, GPU, disk space and operating system), and they are published on the workshop pages. Please check them before registering for a workshop.

items.q: Do I need a teaching assistant?
items.a: Yes. Each workshop should have at least one teaching assistant (TA) to help participants during the practical part.

items.q: How should I structure my workshop?
items.a: Plan a milestone-based progression for the 90 minutes, so participants reach concrete checkpoints. Your proposal must include this breakdown together with a breakdown of the 25-minute morning presentation.

items.q: Do participants register separately for workshops?
items.a: Yes. Workshop seats are registered separately from the conference registration and are limited to the workshop size chosen by the speakers.

items.q: When does registration open?
items.a: Registration opens after the notification of acceptance. Dates are listed on the Important Dates page; subscribe to updates to be notified.

items.q: Can I attend without presenting?
items.a: Yes. Everyone interested in autonomous systems is welcome to register and attend.

items.q: How do I get a visa invitation letter?
items.a: Registered participants can request an invitation letter through the contact form (topic: Visa invitation letter). See the Visa Information page for what to include.

items.q: Where will the conference take place?
items.a: The venue and dates will be announced on the Conference Venue page and in the site header.
